evidence.title: Loudoun Board Enacts Pause on Data Centers
evidence.supports: The Board's pause covers Board consideration of legislative applications for 'data centers and substations' only; describes the scope, exceptions (grid-reliability substations, grandfathered cases), and open-ended/event-based term tied to completion of the Phase 2 Data Center Standards and Locations initiative.
evidence.quote: The Loudoun County Board of Supervisors voted Tuesday to enact a temporary pause on Board consideration of certain legislative applications for data centers and substations

evidence.title: Board Approves Plan to Temporarily Pause Legislative Data Center and Substation Applications
evidence.supports: Confirms the pause is capped at up to 12 months (the Virginia-law statutory maximum for action on such legislative applications) and applies only to data center and electrical substation legislative applications, not to battery storage as a separate use.
evidence.quote: Under the terms of the pause approved by the Board, final votes on data center and substation applications will be paused for one year.

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK resolved: 'battery storage' appears only in the row's trigger field, describing the broader Phase 2 Data Center Standards and Locations initiative's future scope (siting, noise, building heights, on-site power generation, and battery storage standards) -- not in the operative scope of this pause. Both the Board's press release and the official CivicAlert describe the pause itself as covering only 'data center and substation' legislative applications; battery storage facilities are not separately paused. This is a trigger/background mention, not operative coverage, so sectors correctly stays ["data_center"]. No change. Duration_kind (until_event, capped at 'up to one year') and the open-ended framing also checked against both sources and remain accurate as of 2026-09-23.
